section.title: Jack, the Last Word
section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: The brief names the form outright: a memorial, six speakers on their feet, the eulogy's swing between a laugh, an angry line, and a stretch that can barely be got through. Jack is a deliberate exception to strict alternation and to normal voice balance - she opens and closes by the brief's fixed order, so she holds two of the seven turns while Tali, Grunt, Liara, Joker and Wrex each hold one. Her two turns are sized as ordinary single turns rather than doubled, but together they total roughly twice any other voice's word count, which is the "two turns' worth" the brief asks for. Section targets were raised after the voice checkpoint, at the user's instruction to let the speeches run to their natural length rather than be trimmed to a grid; the middle five now sit at 900-1050 and the episode target at 6650. Each middle turn answers the one directly before it; Jack's closing turn answers the whole room, not just Wrex. Grunt's bible is new and unused before this run - he is built distinct from Wrex throughout: Wrex remembers the Rebellions and the genophage firsthand, Grunt states krogan history as Okeer's tank taught it and then flattens it to "put in me, not lived," and his own lived material is small and recent (the Rite, the Citadel, the mess hall, the war) and used in full. The "gets a detail wrong and is corrected" requirement is carried by two beats, not one: Grunt states the assumed version (died on his feet with a gun) and Joker mis-hears whose voice was on the channel, and Wrex corrects both flatly before giving the room the true version - shot on the way to the landing zone, then killed driving a vehicle into a banshee to clear passage for Hammer. Wrex reads that off the wreckage he found days later, not off memory; nobody in the room watched Thomas die, and each of them holds only a piece. No section narrates the Crucible's mechanism or Shepard as confirmed dead; Thomas's Synthesis sympathies, where they surface, are framed as a political stance he held in life, never as knowledge of the ending.

promises: answers the whole room, not just Wrex - picks up something from each of the five turns in between without tidying any of it
the manuscript of poems and the birthday speech he left behind, and what she intends to do with them
says outright, now, what the no-promises rule was for and that both of them broke it - the last confession of the night

he tried to call her at the end and what reached her was an empty voice note, no words on it at all - which inverts their whole long-distance habit, where she was the one who sent voice notes that said almost nothing and he sent the long sincere messages; she has played it more times than she will admit and there is nothing on it to find
closes on anger and unresolved grief, lust, pain and love, not acceptance
Shepard is still missing and there is no closure on offer even here, he knew him longer than anyone, and he should be here

canon.statement: Jack has an N7 tattoo on her ass. After the Grissom Academy escape, Prangley asked her about her tattoos in general, and she mentioned that one specifically just to watch him choke on the question.
canon.overrides: no specific tattoo design or location established in the corpus

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body, so no burial. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.
canon.overrides: shepard_fate = Dead (synthesis) stated as settled fact

canon.statement: Shepard never had a first name. "Shepard" started as a mocking nickname the Tenth Street Reds gave him for his knack with people. He only took a surname because Alliance enlistment required one, and he kept that one as a screw-you to the Reds.
canon.overrides: Earthborn Shepard as the wiki describes it (first name player-chosen, surname by birth)

canon.statement: Shepard got clean of drugs but never stopped loving alcohol and parties. Jack thinks the good-guy act is just that, an act: in her telling he has turned up at every bar in the galaxy and calls each one his favorite, and he drinks and dances every time. He even did it on Omega, where somebody could have poisoned him. She calls him a drunk and a dumbass, and she's fond of him.

canon.statement: Jack is teaching Shepard to loosen up when he dances, and she has dragged him into a mosh pit.

scenes.title: The Party at Shepard's Apartment
scenes.when: 2186, Citadel shore leave, after the clone was stopped and the Normandy retaken, before Cronos Station
scenes.where: Shepard's personal apartment on the Wards — two floors, kitchen, bar by the window, poker den, balcony, hot tub, rock garden

beats.text: Joker suggests the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy. Shepard buys Party Provisions from the kiosk at the bar on the second floor of the Silver Coast Casino for 100 credits, then sends the invitations from the private terminal in the apartment office.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez and Samantha Traynor are automatic. Everyone else is an optional invite, and only surviving squadmates whose Mass Effect 3 arcs are finished can come at all.

Absences nobody explains: Gardner, Allers, Chakwas, Chambers, Adams, Donnelly and Daniels are all missing. Traynor mentions in the kitchen that Chakwas is dealing with a medical emergency on the Citadel. The rest are simply not addressed.
Glyph asks the Commander what kind of party this is — quiet or energetic — and the answer sets the opening conversations. The groupings themselves are set by the guest list, not the theme.

Opening arrangement: Liara and Traynor in the kitchen with Tali, Samara and Garrus. EDI and Joker at the bar by the window with Miranda and Jacob. James and Cortez on the couches by the piano with the Virmire survivor and Jack. Wrex and Grunt upstairs on the balcony with Zaeed and Javik. Kasumi flits between the bar and the kitchen, uncloaking to interject.

Wrex and Grunt spend the opening trading krogan insults over who is stronger — Grunt calling Wrex a fossil and belittling his age. If the mood is energetic they headbutt each other to settle it and Shepard has to stop them before the furniture goes.
Grunt tells Wrex that two of Aralakh Company's recruits had opposed his appointment, and that only one of them had to be dealt with, the other having been killed in a fight.

Garrus's verdict on the place is that it would be a good place to retire, its sightlines appealing to his sniper sensibilities. He complains at a quiet party about the lack of hard drinks and at an energetic one dares Shepard to try the swill on offer.

Traynor cannot get over the size of the apartment — the electric bill alone would have covered her college tuition. Tali's version is that the same bill would have bought her an air conditioner for her suit, which she does not have, and it gets hot in there.
The group toasts the Normandy. Traynor admits she still feels like an outsider next to people who have histories with Shepard, and everyone weighs in.

Traynor gets everyone recounting how they met Shepard. Tali's memory is that all she could think about was hoping Shepard had showered, because her filter needed replacing and humans carry a lot of germs. Liara notes that three years on she is drinking Shepard's booze through a straw, and calls that progress.

Second phase, energetic: Liara and James argue on the balcony about whether biotics or muscle wins, with Jacob, Miranda, Jack, Kaidan and the Virmire survivor taking sides. James shows off his "fine example of peak physical form"; Liara says she is going to challenge him to a pull-up contest, which gives him pause. When James jabs at "flawed implants," Kaidan shoots back with how hard he has worked and his resulting ability to Reave, drawing trepidation from Liara and Jacob. Shepard picks a side. If Shepard backs biotics, Liara lifts him off the floor with no visible effort and Kasumi uncloaks to goad him into sit-ups; if Shepard backs muscle, the push-ups happen instead and Kaidan is flabbergasted, though Shepard can comfort him by saying that his kind of physical excellence is Shepard's kind too.

Second phase, energetic, at the bar: Joker gets ganged up on by Cortez, Garrus, Wrex and Javik or Zaeed over refusing to keep a sidearm in the cockpit. Garrus's line is that a weapon he cannot get to is no weapon at all. Wrex offers Tuchanka as the harshest planet alive and dares anyone present to last a day there, says krogan parties involve a lot of violent deaths, and announces he needs to shoot something. If Shepard keeps the mood up and backs the shooting practice, he makes good on it — bottles on the counter, with Javik and Zaeed joining in.

Second phase, energetic, at the door: Grunt works the vid-phone as bouncer, distinguishing fake salarian lip-hair from the real thing and establishing that Shepard has no half-brother named Sheppy the Volus. He is briefly tempted by cookies and turns them away anyway.

Second phase, quiet: Grunt dares Wrex into a drinking contest and will not accept his excuses, goading him with "logic is for salarians" and the observation that the great Urdnot Wrex has backed down from a challenge. Elsewhere Liara and James compare the SSV Normandy with the SR-2 in the den, with Tali acting out both ships' handling and engine noise and reporting that the SR-2 is harder to perform. Garrus and Zaeed stand on the balcony discussing how to make the apartment defensible. Kaidan, Joker and Samantha discuss EDI on the second floor.
Traynor and Joker — or Traynor and EDI, extremely awkwardly — work through Traynor's recorded opinion of EDI's voice, while Tali nearly poisons herself with cheese trying to change the subject.

Third phase, quiet: Tali ends up on the floor of the downstairs bathroom, wasted and barely comprehensible, having got an omni-tattoo at Jack's suggestion. Shepard tells her to get some rest and hears fragments of her muttering while passing the door afterwards. Grunt is wherever the food or the drink is, announcing his hunger. Liara and James play cards in the den with Javik and a cloaked Kasumi, Glyph dealing if Shepard sends it there.

Third phase, energetic: Grunt is wasted under the running shower upstairs, muttering about being a Space Cowboy, asking whether someone is a wizard, mourning that hanar cannot wear sweaters and reporting that he found a blue rock for Liara. Downstairs the dancing starts between the kitchen and the conference room — Traynor, Cortez, Jack, Samara, Garrus and Tali — with Glyph setting up the floor if sent. Kasumi is in the downstairs bedroom closet going through Shepard's underwear drawer.

Garrus on watching Shepard dance: record it and broadcast it at the Reapers, because they will either run, melt down, or fall in love. Someone starts reciting the periodic table; at "element 69" the humans snicker and Garrus reminds them it is thulium.

Garrus's quiet-party alternative is micro-filaments — tiny explosives laid in a grid across the glass by the door that shred anyone coming through — coordinated with Zaeed over comms, and he later gets to name a booby-trapped coffee maker "caffeine rush".

At the end Shepard assembles everyone by the couch for a group photo. Couples face each other; everyone else looks at the camera. The photograph hangs afterwards by the downstairs bar, opposite the fireplace.

variants.text: Miranda and Jack end up in the den insulting each other. Shepard can push them to reconcile or egg them on; Kasumi uncloaks either way and makes it worse.
Liara calls the apartment the "Shepard-Vakarian love nest"; if Shepard is with someone else, Garrus is the one making the love-nest joke and promising not to interrupt.

Ashley sits with James by the ground-floor couches in the first phase, teasing Cortez. In an energetic second phase, if she and James are both unromanced, James tries to recruit her to his side of the biotics-versus-muscle argument; she flirts back and takes an interest in his physique, and if Shepard encourages the two of them the night pushes them closer without anything coming of it — James tries out a line of Spanish on her that only leaves her asking him to repeat himself. If either of them had been turned down by Shepard first, Ashley alternates between attraction and rejection instead and declines to back James in the argument. During a relaxed third phase, if Wrex is present he recounts being ready to kill for the genophage cure back on Virmire and asks Ashley whether she would have shot him; she says without hesitation that she would have if he'd left her no choice, and Wrex says he respects her for it.

evidence.text: Scan and then pick up each plant sample at the navpoints. - Elaaden - Amanita Jatanum – inside a cave in Languish with a Memory Trigger (west of New Tuchanka) - DATA: Tentative classification: Amanita jatanum. Other submitted names: redbulb mushroom, ember shroom. Nutritional content: Medium - ANALYSIS: Though not poisonous, this mildly psychoactive mushroom has valuable medicinal properties. Extracted agents could be used to enhance medi\-gels pain\-reducing capabilities. - Lagenaria Lunarium – in the shade of a tree next to the building complex in Sea of Ataraxia (west of the westernmost Forward Station) **Note:**  The building next to the plant sample is related to the mission The Rebel. It is advised to start The Rebel mission before visiting this location to acquire that mission first. - DATA: Tentative classification: Lagenaria lunarium. Other submitted names: moon gourd, whitepulp melon. Nutritional content: High - ANALYSIS: A succulent segmented gourd with high water content. The flesh surrounding the seeds could be eaten raw, or sliced and dried for storage. - Eos - Neolecta Riftia – near some rocks in Fairwinds Basin (east of the Forward Station in the middle of the lake) - DATA: Tentative classification: Neolecta riftia. Other submitted names: tubeworm fungus, trumpet plants. Nutritional content: High - ANALYSIS: These fungi should have a pleasant taste from absorbing mineral salts. - Havarl - Lactarius Assefa – mushroom near a tree in Central Wilds (east of the Forward Station). - DATA: Tentative classification: Lactarius assefa. Other submitted names: thatchcap mushroom, soldier's joy. Nutritional content: Extremely high - ANALYSIS: These mushrooms are rich in protein and could quickly bulk out rations, but unless prepared carefully they would have a sour aftertaste. - Sargania Fructanis – on a hill near the outer walls (directly north of the Lactarius Assefa plant) - DATA: Tentative classification: Sargania fructanis. Other submitted names: red\-veined saragras, candy plant. Nutritional content: Medium - ANALYSIS: The stems of this plant produce a red syrup with a surprisingly high sugar content. However, it will stain both armor and teeth if spilled. - Kadara - Diplazium Dizone – near a rock in Draullir (east of the Forward station) - DATA: Tentative classification: Diplazium dizone. Other submitted names: sword fern, stickgrass. Nutritional content: Acceptable - ANALYSIS: Gathered and properly cooked, these plants would provide a tasty source of vitamins and minerals. - Nereocystis Harmonia – by an acid pool east of Ditaeon - DATA: Tentative classification: Nereocystis harmonia. Other submitted names: pearl kelp, thin stem. Nutritional content: Acceptable - ANALYSIS: This plant resembles kelp growths, and may have kelp ancestors. While not especially nutritious, it is vitamin rich and has a pleasantly cleansing taste. - Rheum Taelkarum – on an island in the pools near Kadara Port (north of the Forward Station) - DATA: Tentative classification: Rheum taelkarum. Other submitted names: broad\-leafed taelk, reservoir plant. Nutritional content: Extremely high - ANALYSIS: Both water\-rich and full of nutrients, this attractive plant appears to protect against predators with a peppery taste. This can be countered with an enzyme supplement. - Ruberia Majora – in a shallow acid pool in (east of the Rheum Taelkarum plant) - DATA: Tentative classification: Ruberia majora. Other submitted names: longcoral, crimson longfrond. Nutritional content: Medium - ANALYSIS: This plant has a high protein content, though its tough fibers and thick roots would require a long cooking time. - Voeld - Cardacha Cthonis – in Techiix's vegetation cave - DATA: Tentative classification: Cardacha cthonis. Other submitted names: thulus stem, octopus plant. Nutritional content: High - ANALYSIS: Despite its appearance, this plant has extremely nutritious seeds tucked into the stem coil. The stem is also water\-rich and could be easily peeled. - In the room with the Cardacha Cthonis, Ryder can scan a Storage Climate Control for \+10 .

evidence.text:
This Shadow Broker dossier, unlocked after the Lair of the Shadow Broker mission, covered Jack, called "Subject Zero." The Broker noted her abnormal biotic power compared favorably with the Pragia (Teltin) facility's expected results and that she was easily manipulated through emotional impairment caused by childhood abuse and confinement.

An extranet log shows she avoided the Normandy's connection and used a private omni-tool line, searching Citadel Newsnet archives for Cerberus, Pragia, Teltin, the Illusive Man and Miranda Lawson, watching footage of the geth attacks on Eden Prime and the Citadel (and closing Shepard's Spectre inauguration after twelve seconds), studying escape-pod procedures, mass relay maps and no-flight zones, and being banned from a news forum for swearing and from Galactic Champion Poker 2100 after an altercation. She then wiped her history with a commercial VI.

An intercepted message is a rejection from Galactic Poetry Monthly addressed to "Jacqueline Nought," reproducing her submitted poem, which ends: "I mark myself / Black and jagged / To cover the scars / That make me a monster / A warning / This is not a place of honor / No esteemed dead are buried here."

A surveillance transcript from the Helios Medical Facility on Eden Prime, dated 2165 and tapped for possible Cerberus involvement, records Doctor Castor telling a mother that her infant daughter died of seizures from prenatal element zero exposure, one of several such deaths the facility had seen, and blaming government inaction on treatments that might "interfere with their biotic recruitments." Castor persuades the grieving woman to donate the body "for tests," then opens a secure channel: "I've got a candidate... highest potential I've seen in years... No, the family has been dealt with. Send a team from Pragia ASAP." The page's trivia notes the inconsistency between this 2165 "baby" and the Cerberus dossier's listed 2161 birth year for Subject Zero.

evidence.text:
Ereba was an asari merchant. In Mass Effect 2 she ran Memories of Illium, a store on Illium selling model starships and fish, and was the object of the affections of the love-struck krogan Charr, who stood nearby reciting poetry. Ereba had been in a relationship with Charr but broke it off because she was unsure what she wanted, and suspected he was mainly interested in her for children, noting that krogan affected by the genophage sometimes procreate only with asari. Commander Shepard could persuade her either to take Charr back or to forget him; in either case she gave Shepard a store discount. If Shepard reunited them, the couple traveled to Tuchanka to start a new life, where Ereba doubted the ramshackle settlement and the xenophobia of other krogan and wanted to leave, but Charr convinced her to stay under his protection.

By 2186, in Mass Effect 3, Ereba worked on the Citadel in the Presidium Commons as a merchant for Nos Astra Sporting Goods. If Shepard had kept her with Charr, she was married to him and mentioned to a customer that he was off fighting the Reapers. Should Shepard pursue a missing krogan team, the Commander could recover a dying message from Charr consisting mostly of poetry with references to an unborn child, which he asked be brought to Ereba; on hearing it played back she was shaken and excused herself. If Shepard had broken the couple up or ignored their troubles, Ereba was instead overheard discussing the war on Palaven, but Charr still left a message for her, which Shepard could deliver or withhold; she was still rattled if it was delivered.

In Mass Effect 2 cut content, Ereba had a few ambient voicelines, since removed, in which she was clearly annoyed at Charr's poetry.

evidence.text:
"Aria: Eclipse" was a Mass Effect 3 mission, part of Aria T'Loak's trilogy of tasks to unite mercenary bands under her control in exchange for the Terminus Fleet War Asset. It became available after Priority: Palaven, once the primarch had been retrieved from Palaven, by speaking with Aria at the Purgatory bar on the Citadel. It was written by Neil Pollner.

Aria sent Shepard to secure the release of the jailed Eclipse founder and leader Jona Sederis. Commander Bailey, at the Citadel Embassies, insisted that Shepard speak with Sederis first; Shepard did so via a vidcomm conversation at the Presidium Commons C-Sec outpost, gaining morality points. Afterward, Shepard could either pressure Bailey to release Sederis, which ended the mission with Sederis resuming command of Eclipse, or track down her salarian second-in-command Sayn, who led the band in her absence.

Sayn was found in the processing area of the Docks holding area, near the Shepard VI, where he was plotting to break Sederis out of prison. Shepard could remind him that he was currently in charge and convince him either to let Sederis rot in jail or to have her killed upon her "release." Either way, Sayn took over. Regardless of the outcome, the Eclipse leadership submitted to Aria's authority, the Terminus Fleet War Asset was updated by 50 points, and Shepard received 210 experience, 5,000 credits, and morality points. A bug could softlock the mission and Aria's entire tri-mission arc if the player saved and quit immediately after talking to Sayn.
evidence.for_key: Jack's poetry, written and submitted anonymously

evidence.text:
Subject Zero was a passive class power used exclusively by the squad member Jack in the single-player modes of Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3. The page described it as a game mechanic representing Jack's self-experimentation with her unusual biotic abilities.

In Mass Effect 2 the power enhanced Jack's health and weapon damage while reducing the recharge time of her powers, scaling upward across its first three ranks. At Rank 4 it evolved into one of two specializations: Primal Adept, which pushed her biotics to their limit for the greatest reduction in power recharge time, or Primal Vanguard, which focused her energy into combat for the highest weapon damage bonus.

In Mass Effect 3 the power was rebuilt with six ranks. It boosted health and shield bonuses alongside power recharge speed, with later ranks offering choices between recharge speed and durability, between weapon damage and increased power force and duration, and between a squad-wide biotic recharge bonus and a further personal recharge boost. In both games the power was available only to Jack and was not offered in multiplayer.

evidence.page: The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy/Mass Effect 2
evidence.text: These images are production paintings showing Jack in her element, giving a feel for what she can do when she breaks out of *Purgatory*. Jack is a punk, and early variations focused on that. Her pants, which were part of her prison uniform, were rolled down to reflect Jack's unique sense of style. Her tattoos cover her scars in a deliberate attempt to write her own story, erasing the pain of her past. An actress's head was scanned to serve as the model for Jack's face. It was decided that Jack needed a shaved head for a genuine punk feel rather than making her a supermodel with ink. Once it was decided that Jack would be clothed in tattoos, various directions were explored for how to tell her backstory through them. We also sought ways to best show off her tattoos while covering her chest to some degree. Concerns about how exposed she was led to some of the changes.

evidence.text:
Citadel: Party was a Mass Effect 3 mission in the Citadel DLC in which Commander Shepard hosted a gathering at the Personal Apartment during shore leave. Joker suggested the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy SR-2 in Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy. To prepare, Shepard bought Party Provisions for 100 credits, or 90 with both Intel Terminal discounts, from a kiosk at the Silver Coast Casino bar, then sent invitations from the apartment's private terminal. The party had to be held before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters, after which the DLC content closed.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez, and Samantha Traynor were auto-invited as guaranteed survivors. All other guests were optional and required surviving all three games with their Mass Effect 3 arcs complete: Garrus, Grunt, Jacob, Jack, Javik, Kasumi, Samara, Zaeed, Wrex, Ashley or Kaidan, Tali, and Miranda Lawson, each with specific prerequisites. Squadmates fated to die in their arcs, Legion and Thane Krios, did not appear; Mordin Solus would not break cover even if he survived; Morinth was absent. Other Normandy crew such as Karin Chakwas could not attend, with Traynor stating Chakwas was handling a medical emergency on the Citadel.

Glyph asked Shepard to pick a Quiet or Energetic theme, which set dialogue but not group arrangements. The party ran in phases: an opening, a second part where Shepard could keep or switch the theme and settle guest disagreements, and a final phase whose arrangements followed the second theme, with Shepard choosing which group Glyph joined. Kasumi repeatedly uncloaked to interject. Conversations covered the two Normandys, biotics versus muscle, Joker's refusal to keep a gun in the cockpit, and Miranda and Jack's feuding. The phase ended with a Group Photo, later hung near the downstairs bar, in which romantic couples faced each other.

Shepard woke in the aftermath, potentially beside a love interest; an unromanced female Shepard could wake with James Vega or Javik. If Mordin had survived through the genophage arc, a datapad of his recordings lay by the bed. The guests dispersed around the apartment before Shepard signaled Rapid Transit to return everyone to Docking Bay D24. The Normandy crew gathered at the observation window; if Shepard had romanced Thane, his spirit appeared to speak to his siha before Shepard boarded last, closing the DLC. The Silversun Strip remained accessible afterward. Mark Meer later said Shepard's final franchise line, recorded for this mission, was "The best."
evidence.for_key: Jack's tattoos and the Citadel party

evidence.text: - In Mass Effect 2, Jack was written by Brian Kindregan, including most of her confrontation with Miranda, while some late edits were orchestrated by Lukas Kristjanson after Kindregan's departure. - Concept art on Jack's tattoos figure backstories for several of the designs. Jack's "murdered sisters" were apparently based on prototype designs for her own appearance. - The Shadow Broker dossier on Cerberus lists the birth year of "Subject Zero" as 2161\. However, in the dossier on Jack herself, the surveillance log of the Helios Medical Facility dated 2165 contains references to her as a "baby" and an "infant", words that aren't normally used to describe a child at 3\-4 years old. - Courtenay Taylor, who voiced Jack, also voiced the Cathar Jedi Juhani in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic as well as Farinden and Shaevra in BioWare's Dragon Age: Origins. - Jack periodically yells "I will destroy you!" and "I'll kill you!" when in combat and/or using abilities. This may be a reference to the combat barks used by humanoid enemies in Mass Effect or by Juhani in Knights of the Old Republic. - Jack's name and shaved head might be a reference to the character Jack/Kyra from the *Chronicles of Riddick* movie series, more specifically the first movie *Pitch Black*, in which the character was approximately 14 years of age. The two characters also share similarities in that they are both killers and are found in prison, which they both escape from with the help of the protagonist. - According to the Shadow Broker's dossier on her, she has used the name Jacqueline Nought on at least one occasion. That name also appears on the memorial wall in Mass Effect 3 if Jack was killed on the Suicide Mission (which is the case in an unmodified game of Mass Effect 3 that was not imported from a Mass Effect 2 save file). "Jacqueline" is a typically feminine counterpart to "Jack," and "nought" is an English word meaning "nothing" or "zero". - During the car chase scene in the Lair of the Shadow Broker DLC, a wanted poster of Jack can be seen displayed on a large advertising screen above a tunnel. She is displayed with the prisoner number 24601. - If brought along on the mission Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation, Liara reveals that Jack's birth name is "Jennifer" and offers to find out her last name if she asks politely. |  | **The following information is drawn from cut content and is not to be considered canon in any way.** | | --- | --- |

evidence.page: The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy/Mass Effect 2
evidence.text:
This page transcribes the Mass Effect 2 section of the developer commentary in the 2021 edition of The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy, with text credited to Casey Hudson, Derek Watts, Chris Hepler, Karin Weekes and Ryan Cormier. It is a behind-the-scenes reference collecting BioWare's notes on the concept art and design process for the game.

The commentary walks through character designs for Commander Shepard's piece-based armor, Jacob Taylor, Miranda Lawson, Garrus Vakarian, Tali'Zorah, Grunt, Thane Krios, Mordin Solus, Legion, Jack, Samara, the Illusive Man, and DLC companions Kasumi Goto and Zaeed Massani. It records design intentions such as krogan crests growing with age, Thane's balaclava evoking a ski mask, Jack's tattoos covering her scars, the Illusive Man's deliberately "inhuman" eye implants, and Zaeed's abandoned prosthetic-leg and dog concepts.

Enemy and creature entries cover the Scion, Praetorian, Proto-Reaper (built from harvested human DNA), and the insect-inspired Collectors, plus the YMIR, FENRIS and LOKI mechs, the Oculus (referencing HAL 9000) and the engineer's tech drone.

Environment sections describe Omega (shaped like a mushroom cloud, with Afterlife modeled on Las Vegas clubs), Illium's utopian Nos Astra, the Citadel Wards, Tuchanka, Horizon, 2175 Aeia, the prison ship Purgatory, Pragia, the Migrant Fleet and its liveships (with a note that quarians follow a vegan diet for water-conservation reasons), Korlus, the Lazarus Research Station, the Derelict Reaper, and the Collector Ship.

The Normandy SR-2 entry explains that the plot's requirement to destroy the original ship freed the team to redesign it with multiple floors, a "muscle car" paint job and a supercollider-style engine room. Weaponry notes cover the five conventional gun classes and the new heavy weapons. DLC sections address Arrival (originally an underwater base inspired by The Abyss), Kasumi – Stolen Memory, Zaeed – The Price of Revenge, Lair of the Shadow Broker (including the Shadow Broker's dual human/alien design), Overlord and David Archer, and Project Firewalker with the M-44 Hammerhead derived from the Mako.

evidence.text:
This page transcribes all commentary texts from the Mass Effect 2 Art Book published in 2010; the writers are unattributed. The texts are organized into five sections describing the game's concept art and design intentions.

"Heroes and Villains" covers character design: several characters were born from production paintings, including the Illusive Man, whose impeccable futuristic suit was meant to convey the swagger of a charming billionaire. Grunt was given smoother horns and showroom-new armor to contrast with other krogan; Garrus would bear scars and bandages from a near-fatal injury for most of the story; Miranda was reconceived from blonde to black hair to suit the "femme fatale" look; Jack's tattoos told a visual story of her past; Samara's armor captured a "mystic warrior" archetype; Legion gained moving parts for expression and Shepard's N7 armor became integral to its appearance and backstory; Mordin balanced brilliant scientist with combat tech specialist; Tali's look was made more mature; and Thane had to be a sleek alien assassin and an attractive love interest.

"Alien Life Forms" describes the hybridization of humans and Reaper technology through escalating enemies culminating in the Reaper-human larva, whose designs spanned Reaper and human forms before a partially-formed human shape of Reaper construction was chosen. Scions were crude fusions of Reaper technology and human anatomy; Collectors were inspired by electron microscope photographs of insect heads; and Praetorians fused Collector DNA with multiple human heads. "Alien Worlds" covers the Citadel, Cerberus interiors and Minuteman Station, Illium, Purgatory, Korlus ("junk world"), and Omega, whose shape was inspired by a nuclear mushroom cloud, with Collector interiors drawing on bee hives. "Transport" covers the quarian Migrant Fleet's tadpole-like ships, the Collector ship inspired by Australian termite mounds, the new squad shuttle, the Hammerhead-reimagined Mako, the Gunship, and the Cerberus-built Normandy SR-2, which was meant to feel like a crude knockoff but ended up luxurious with wood inlay and leather seats. "Weapons" covers heavy weapons including the Collector beam weapon and the tactical nuke.

evidence.text: Ben signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the aliens' bombardment of Shanxi's settlements. A master of munitions, he was a perfect recruit for Jack's prohumanity movement. Eventually he, Jack, and Eva formed a mercenary trio conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and he served as Jack's right\-hand man.

evidence.text:
Terra Firma was a human political party that opposed humanity's growing integration into the galactic community, holding that humanity needed to stand alone to remain strong. Members cited Shanxi and the First Contact War as proof that aliens could not be trusted, marked Armistice Day with an annual protest, and opposed the teaching of alien languages in schools. The party was founded after first contact with the turians, when humans learned how many races made up Citadel space, out of genuine concern that human individuality might be diluted. Its manifesto was not especially extremist, but it attracted xenophobes and reactionaries, and it declined to curb its members' racist rhetoric on free-speech grounds.

In Mass Effect: Ascension (2173), Terra Firma was caught in a kickback scandal involving Nashan Stellar Dynamics, forcing party leader Inez Simmons to resign. Leadership candidates Charles Saracino and Claude Menneau campaigned vigorously; Menneau led the polls by three points until he vanished en route to a rally on Shanxi, his ship and crew never found. With his rival gone, Saracino ran unopposed and was elected party leader.

In Mass Effect, Commander Shepard could discuss the party with Ashley Williams aboard the Normandy; uncomfortable around aliens herself, Ashley reacted angrily to comparisons with Terra Firma, calling its members jackals who had strayed from the founders' ideals. Shepard could also encounter a Terra Firma protest on the Citadel led by Saracino himself during the assignment Citadel: Our Own Worst Enemy, where Saracino, seeking a political seat, asked Shepard to endorse him. "Terra firma" is Latin for "solid Earth." A Shadow Broker dossier later listed the Illusive Man's liaisons Staci and Stephi Strong as the "Terra Firma Twins."

evidence.text: Glyph accompanies Liara throughout Shepard's identity theft fiasco. It purchases tickets and make reservations to a fundraiser on the Silver Coast Casino that has a lead on Shepard's situation, and later reports activity at the Citadel Archives. As Shepard brings the entire team out on a mission, Glyph follows into the archives as well. It gets repeatedly confused by Shepard's clone, as well as sidetracked by various historical information held in the archives, such as information on elcor mating rituals. During fights, Liara instructs Glyph to lower the enemy's morale. It hovers over various targets and tells them statistical data on the likelihood of their survival, as well as various benefits that come with joining the Alliance military. Glyph later helps free Shepard and the squad when they are trapped and abandoned in iridium vaults by the clone and Maya Brooks. Glyph helps Shepard organize a party in the aftermath of the clone incident. When the party gets going at the Personal Apartment, Glyph adds a bow\-tie to its holographic avatar, and asks Shepard what mood to set for the party. If Shepard set the ambience for a quiet party, Glyph can either help with food or drink preparation. It accompanies Samantha Traynor in either case. If a loud party is chosen instead, Glyph can either observe the guests dancing at the balcony or the people playing poker downstairs. Whichever way the party ends, it is used to take a photograph of the gang.

evidence.text: The idea for James Vega was to create a blue\-collar military officer\-\-a heavily muscled tank of a man. We gave his armor more heft to imply that James is an unstoppable force. The team added a beard, scars, and tattoos to make him stand out from the other Alliance marines, notably Ash and Kaidan, who are both very clean cut.

evidence.text: Because Jack's biotics emphasize low damage crowd control powers, you may want to balance her with either a weapons\-expert squadmate or an armor\-stripping tech expert, depending on Shepard's own specialties. On higher difficulty levels everything in here has armor and most regenerate, so someone with fire\-related powers will shine. Someone with Warp will help in both of these areas as well, with the added potential for detonating Jack's Pull. An area effect armor\-stripping ability such as Incineration Blast will render crowds of charging varren instantly vulnerable to Jack's Pull, itself preferably upgraded to a Pull Field. Several of the fights in this mission happen at close quarters, where Grunt excels. In terms of heavy weapons, the M\-622 Avalanche, Arc Projector, and M\-490 Blackstorm tend to be most useful for their ability to hit enemies around corners or behind cover. The Arc Projector has unique anti\-krogan properties that can help especially during one encounter.

evidence.text:
This page covers combat tactics for fighting Tela Vasir, the asari Spectre and Shadow Broker agent faced as the boss of Lair of the Shadow Broker in Mass Effect 2. After a skycar chase around Illium's skyways ends with her crashing into Hotel Azure, a bleeding Vasir takes a hostage and then fights Shepard's team in a plaza, eventually succumbing to her wounds after a protracted battle.

Vasir is described as one of the toughest straight-up fights in the game. Offensively she wields an M-15 Vindicator, uses Shockwave to knock targets out of cover, summons reinforcements of Shadow Broker Engineers and Rocket Drones, and has an extra-powerful, wide-radius Biotic Charge with a long charge time that can be interrupted. Defensively her barrier (stronger than a Praetorian's) and armor are extraordinarily strong, and she repeatedly Charge-teleports around the battlefield. Once her defenses are down she becomes vulnerable to biotics such as Pull, Throw and Dominate, to force effects like Concussive Shot and Tech Armor detonation, and to freezing. She is largely stun-resistant while protected, immune to Flashbang Grenade and the Arc Projector stun, and immune to the hold effects of Singularity and the M-490 Blackstorm until only her health remains.

Recommended tactics include using Liara's Stasis (which can stun Vasir even through her protections and can end waves early), Jack's Warp Ammo against her barrier, anti-barrier weapons such as the Collector Particle Beam or Geth Plasma Shotgun, and knocking her off the edge of the map for an instant kill. Class-specific advice is given for Vanguard, Soldier, Engineer, Sentinel, Infiltrator and Adept.
evidence.for_key: Jack's anti-authoritarian politics and her view of institutions

evidence.text: Requires: Jack's survival in the Suicide Mission and completing Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation. **Military Strength:** 25 Jack, formerly known as Subject Zero, may be the most talented biotic of her time. After helping Shepard destroy the Collectors, she was offered a teaching position at Grissom Academy by the Alliance. Accepting the position for reasons of her own, Jack continued to hone her skills while training her students. Grissom Board of Directors member Kahlee Sanders has vouched for Jack's energetic, if unorthodox, teaching style, impressed with the inroads made with the children under the rogue biotic's care.

evidence.section: *09/17/2010 \- Erlan Golta Clashes with Bryan Theodor on "Eye on the Stars"*
evidence.text: *“Political commentator Erlan Golta clashed today with Bryan Theodor, host of the popular late\-night "Eye on the Stars." Golta appeared on the show to discuss his new book "Juggling the Monkeys: An Insider's View of the Tower." When Theodor accused Golta of being deliberately inflammatory in his portrayal of Council politics, Golta said "Are you kidding? I could show you signed orders drawn up to book Commander Shepard on obstruction of justice. And this is from the offices of the Councilors after the \[expletive] Battle of the Citadel." Messages both condemning and applauding the controversial writer have flooded in. When asked about Golta's guest appearance, Theodor remarked "It's always a pleasure. Anytime Golta wants to be catastrophically wrong in front of millions of viewers, I'm happy to have him on."”*

evidence.text: Aria had a colourful past prior to her arrival on Omega. When she did arrive on the station, she worked as an exotic dancer at the Afterlife Club. However, this was merely a clever cover for Aria. Eventually, she overthrew the owner of the Afterlife Club and claimed ownership. She continued to form alliances and consolidate power before finally overthrowing the 'ruler' of Omega: the krogan she deposed, whom she derisively named The Patriarch, was spared as an example of her power to others. Aria is very authoritarian in her reign over Omega, ruling the station with an iron fist. Her organization is quite strong and her men extremely loyal. Almost nothing that happens on Omega escapes her notice, causing mercenary groups to think twice before crossing her. No matter who she deals with, she makes sure she has the upper hand in the bargaining. She has centuries of experience dealing with people who thought themselves being in better positions. Simply by observing a person, she can easily read a lot about them and usually immediately knows when they are lying. She is determined to always get the last word in a conversation, reinforcing her position and authority as Omega's ruler. Aria has commando training and is a very powerful biotic. She has survived for over a thousand years not by needlessly exposing herself to risk; she has the patience and cautiousness to see long\-term plans through. |  | ***“I know when something's not right.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Incursion** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: After speaking with Legion, Tali believes the quarians could sue for peace with the geth. But once Daro'Xen turns Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali has no choice but to support it — "for the good of the Fleet." Her time back among the Fleet regresses her, out of necessity, toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2. She is a victim of politics again, and this time largely powerless.

evidence.text:
Home Away was a flower-shaped luxury space station in Earth orbit, owned by the HOME Group and partially funded by UNIN. It was marketed as a safe, local, small-business alternative to distant planetary colonization ventures, offering residents a perpetual view of Earthrise, high-end VIs, and domestic mechs. Its design echoed the Citadel but with several dozen docking-ring platforms instead of five large arms. Though delicate-looking, it was reinforced with carbon nanofilaments, and each platform had landscaped greenery, artificial water, and multi-level residences beneath mass effect fields, one even featuring a snow-capped hill. Its eezo drive core was rated above class-two and subject to Citadel inspection because of the government funding.

The station's mechs were plated against standard energy weapons and run by a Synthetic Insights SleepEasy Series security VI, backed by turrets, anti-personnel weaponry, and paramilitary troops. Internal comms were mostly unsecured because defenses were built against remote cyberattack rather than intruders arriving in person; facial recognition was extranet-linked in case of infiltration. As a real-estate station it had no anti-spacecraft defenses, only construction-grade debris-clearing weapons.

In Mass Effect Andromeda: Initiation, software stolen from the Andromeda Initiative was stored at one of Home Away's data centers. It proved to be an artificial intelligence kernel that had merged with the station VI, creating a "fake AI" that took control of human-looking combat cyborgs built with tech from Quiet Eddy to stop the intruder Cora Harper from leaving; she and her team escaped explosively, and afterward no residents were reported aware of the infiltration. Cora's team had entered disguised as government inspectors, and one infiltrator actually performed the overdue inspection of the station's eezo converters. The Silhaus family owned a California hacienda-style villa on one platform, complete with shuttle pad, garden, teardrop pool, and security drones, where Alec Ryder confronted UNIN delegate Alis Silhaus during his investigation into the repeated theft of his kernel.
evidence.for_key: Jack's anti-authoritarian politics and her view of institutions

evidence.text:
Ben Hislop was a human mercenary and munitions master who appeared in Mass Effect: Evolution. He signed up to fight turians after his brother was killed during the turian bombardment of Shanxi's settlements during the First Contact War, and fought in the resistance on occupied Shanxi. Recruited into Jack Harper's prohumanity movement, he formed a mercenary trio with Jack and Eva Coré, conducting guerrilla warfare under the employ of General Williams, and served as Jack's right-hand man.

On Shanxi, Ben's unit ambushed a turian patrol and he personally fought and captured the turian general Desolas Arterius with Jack's help. He wanted to execute Desolas but Jack kept the general alive for interrogation. On a mission to find the artifact Desolas sought, Ben antagonized him while Jack's scheme defeated the turian subordinates. Reaching the artifact inside a cave, Ben and Jack were ambushed by hooded figures revealed to be cyberized turians, which proved freakishly strong. When Ben touched the artifact to try to shut it off, he was electrocuted; Jack pried him free but was also affected, leaving both incapacitated. Desolas seized them and ordered Ben's body taken for study.

When Harper and Eva pursued Desolas to Illium, they found Ben alive but mutated into a synthetic form like the "meta-turians." He retained some sense of his identity but followed orders from Desolas and Saren, bringing the artifact, the Arca Monolith, to Palaven, where Desolas tried to replicate Harper's enhancement without creating mindless husks. The artifact commanded Ben to excavate a second artifact to accelerate the transformation. When Eva tried to haul Ben out and then to destroy the artifact, it commanded Ben to slam her head against a wall, killing her. Coming to his senses, a horrified Ben charged Desolas and rammed him into the artifact before he could shoot Harper; Saren tore Desolas away. Prolonged contact with the released energy instantly killed Ben, and his body was later vaporized when Saren ordered an orbital bombardment of the temple. Harper later included Ben's and Eva's names in his manifesto as he became the Illusive Man.

warnings: Thomas is the subject but is not in the corpus: no scene record will ever list them in `participants` or `heard_by`, so a record's silence is not absence. Their presence comes from config/narrators/thomas.notes.md, by its timeline stretches rather than its named occasions — where those notes put them with the crew they were at that period's occasions too, and outside those stretches they were not there. The notes still bind absolutely on the load-bearing facts: relationships, habits, dates, deaths, deeds.
